memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Avery selected the available standard queen room as the practical, lower-total option for the current one-room stay; no broader preference was stated.

messages.content: Now I need the hotel for Chicago. The stay is Tuesday, October 14 through Saturday morning, four nights. I need to be at the museum by 7:00 a.m. Wednesday, and the approved cap is $245 per night before tax.

I’ll compare available rooms for those exact dates and keep the first-morning trip to the downtown museum practical. One detail: the last flight discussion had you leaving Friday night. Has the return moved to Saturday?
Yes. The museum added a Saturday closeout, so the return was changed to Saturday afternoon. Use the four-night stay.

Understood. For October 14–18, I found three workable options near the museum. The Lakeshore Central is $229 nightly, about a 9-minute walk, with a four-night room subtotal of $916. The Wabash House is $214 nightly, roughly 13 minutes on foot, subtotal $856. The Dearborn Plaza is $239 nightly and about 18 minutes by train or 12–20 minutes by car that early, subtotal $956. All are currently within the nightly cap before taxes.
What room types are actually available at the first two, and what do the totals look like after taxes and fees?

At Lakeshore Central, a standard room with one queen bed is available at $229 per night; the estimated total is $1,071.84 including taxes, with no separate destination fee shown. A room with one king is $241 nightly and totals about $1,128.00. At Wabash House, the available standard room has one king bed at $214 nightly; after taxes and a $20 nightly facility fee, the estimated total is $1,081.52. The fee includes Wi-Fi and fitness-room access.
So Wabash has the lower base rate but ends up costing more than the queen room at Lakeshore?

Correct. Wabash is $15 less per night on the advertised rate, but its facility fee pushes the estimated four-night total $9.68 above Lakeshore Central. Lakeshore also has the shorter and simpler walk for the 7:00 a.m. call.
Check cancellation terms and whether either one charges the first night now.

The Lakeshore Central queen room can be canceled without penalty until 6:00 p.m. local time on Sunday, October 12. After that, the penalty is one night plus tax. A card guarantee is required, but the hotel indicates payment is due at check-in. Wabash House allows free cancellation until 3:00 p.m. on Monday, October 13, but it charges a one-night deposit when booked; that deposit becomes nonrefundable after the deadline.
Lakeshore seems better for this job. Is the walk straightforward before dawn, or would I be depending on transit?

It is a direct street-level walk of about 0.4 mile, with no transfer or transit schedule involved. The hotel’s main entrance is staffed around the clock. Allowing extra time for signals and the staff entrance at the museum, leaving around 6:40 a.m. should be reasonable.
Choose the standard queen at Lakeshore Central. Keep it within the approved amount and note the cancellation deadline, but don’t book until I send the final travel authorization.

Selected, not booked: Lakeshore Central, standard room with one queen bed, checking in Tuesday, October 14 and checking out Saturday, October 18. The rate is $229 per night before tax, within the $245 cap; the estimated four-night total is $1,071.84. It is about a 9-minute walk from the museum, and free cancellation is available until 6:00 p.m. Chicago time on Sunday, October 12. Availability and price can change until the reservation is confirmed.

updated_continuity_summary: Avery is planning a one-person Atlanta–Chicago museum work trip for October 14–18. The museum added a Saturday closeout, and the return has moved to Saturday afternoon. She must reach the downtown museum by 1:00 p.m. Tuesday for a crate handoff and report for a 7:00 a.m. installation call Wednesday. One standard checked installation-tool case is included; it weighs about 42 pounds, and its removable drill battery will travel in hand luggage. A standard room at Lakeshore Central has been selected for four nights at $229 per night before tax, estimated at $1,071.84 total, with free cancellation until 6:00 p.m. Chicago time on October 12. The hotel and flight itinerary remain unpurchased pending final travel authorization.
